messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Vector Network Analyzer solution with a competitor for Semiconductor without making unsupported claims?

The passages do not provide a supported Semiconductor VNA comparison between R&S and a competitor; they only show that the Semiconductor knowledge base has a VNA sub-index, not a competitor comparison claim.[9]
To compare without unsupported claims, you need the exact competitor model, frequency range, option codes, calibration kit or TDR option, because the Keysight ENA source does not provide those details.[12]
To compare without unsupported claims, you also need the competitor performance metrics, because the Keysight ENA source does not provide measurement accuracy, dynamic range, or bandwidth.[12]
The same missing evidence applies to Keysight PNA: the source does not list a specific PNA model, frequency range, option code, calibration kit, or TDR option.[17]
The same missing evidence applies to Keysight PNA performance, because the source does not provide measurement accuracy, dynamic range, or bandwidth.[17]
You need competitor test conditions for Delta-L, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction, because the Keysight ENA source does not state those test conditions.[14]
You need competitor test conditions for Delta-L, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction, because the Keysight PNA source does not state those test conditions.[19]
You may cite only that Keysight ENA/PNA are listed as platforms for material measurement, Delta-L loss, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction in the referenced PCB test-flow context.[10][11][15][16]
For the R&S side, you need the exact R&S VNA model and option set, because the R&S ZNB3000 source lists different base units from 9 kHz to 4.5 GHz, 20 GHz, 32 GHz, and 43.5 GHz, with 2-port and 4-port variants.[20]
For the R&S side, you need the applicable R&S measurement conditions, because ZNB3000 specifications require defined warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration interval, internal adjustments, temperature range, matching measurement and calibration settings, and no interpolation for measurement accuracy.[25]
For the R&S side, you need comparable metric conditions, because ZNB3000 dynamic range is specified at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth without user correction applied, and 1 Hz bandwidth can increase dynamic range.[25]
For the R&S ZNA67EXT side, you need the exact system configuration, because its specifications apply only when operated as a 1.0 mm VNA system with the required configuration matching the rear-panel designation scheme.[29]
For the R&S ZNA67EXT side, you need the option evidence if claiming TDR, extended time-domain analysis, Delta-L PCB characterization, or 110 GHz operation, because the listed options include ZNA-K2, ZNA-K20, ZNA-K231, and ZNA67-K110.[31]
For the R&S ZNL side, you need the exact model and frequency range, because ZNL3, ZNL4, ZNL6, ZNL14, and ZNL20 cover 5 kHz to 3 GHz, 4.5 GHz, 6 GHz, 14 GHz, and 20 GHz respectively.[62]
For the R&S ZNL side, you need the applicable measurement conditions, because ZNL measurement accuracy is valid only under stated temperature, calibration, calibration-kit, frequency-point, bandwidth, sweep-time, and no-interpolation conditions.[62]
【推論】A defensible Semiconductor competitor comparison would require one cited source tying the Semiconductor use case to the R&S VNA configuration and one cited source tying the same Semiconductor use case to the named competitor configuration, because the current Semiconductor passage only shows an index and the current Keysight passages only give PCB-context ENA/PNA mentions with missing model, option, condition, and performance data.[9][10][11][12][14][15][16][17][19]

The passages do not provide a supported Semiconductor VNA comparison between R&S and a competitor; they only show that the Semiconductor knowledge base has a VNA sub-index, not a competitor comparison claim.[9]
To compare without unsupported claims, you need the exact competitor model, frequency range, option codes, calibration kit or TDR option, because the Keysight ENA source does not provide those details.[12]
To compare without unsupported claims, you also need the competitor performance metrics, because the Keysight ENA source does not provide measurement accuracy, dynamic range, or bandwidth.[12]
The same missing evidence applies to Keysight PNA: the source does not list a specific PNA model, frequency range, option code, calibration kit, or TDR option.[17]
The same missing evidence applies to Keysight PNA performance, because the source does not provide measurement accuracy, dynamic range, or bandwidth.[17]
You need competitor test conditions for Delta-L, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction, because the Keysight ENA source does not state those test conditions.[14]
You need competitor test conditions for Delta-L, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction, because the Keysight PNA source does not state those test conditions.[19]
You may cite only that Keysight ENA/PNA are listed as platforms for material measurement, Delta-L loss, TDR impedance measurement, and Dk/Df extraction in the referenced PCB test-flow context.[10][11][15][16]
For the R&S side, you need the exact R&S VNA model and option set, because the R&S ZNB3000 source lists different base units from 9 kHz to 4.5 GHz, 20 GHz, 32 GHz, and 43.5 GHz, with 2-port and 4-port variants.[20]
For the R&S side, you need the applicable R&S measurement conditions, because ZNB3000 specifications require defined warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration interval, internal adjustments, temperature range, matching measurement and calibration settings, and no interpolation for measurement accuracy.[25]
For the R&S side, you need comparable metric conditions, because ZNB3000 dynamic range is specified at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth without user correction applied, and 1 Hz bandwidth can increase dynamic range.[25]
For the R&S ZNA67EXT side, you need the exact system configuration, because its specifications apply only when operated as a 1.0 mm VNA system with the required configuration matching the rear-panel designation scheme.[29]
For the R&S ZNA67EXT side, you need the option evidence if claiming TDR, extended time-domain analysis, Delta-L PCB characterization, or 110 GHz operation, because the listed options include ZNA-K2, ZNA-K20, ZNA-K231, and ZNA67-K110.[31]
For the R&S ZNL side, you need the exact model and frequency range, because ZNL3, ZNL4, ZNL6, ZNL14, and ZNL20 cover 5 kHz to 3 GHz, 4.5 GHz, 6 GHz, 14 GHz, and 20 GHz respectively.[62]
For the R&S ZNL side, you need the applicable measurement conditions, because ZNL measurement accuracy is valid only under stated temperature, calibration, calibration-kit, frequency-point, bandwidth, sweep-time, and no-interpolation conditions.[62]
【推論】A defensible Semiconductor competitor comparison would require one cited source tying the Semiconductor use case to the R&S VNA configuration and one cited source tying the same Semiconductor use case to the named competitor configuration, because the current Semiconductor passage only shows an index and the current Keysight passages only give PCB-context ENA/PNA mentions with missing model, option, condition, and performance data.[9][10][11][12][14][15][16][17][19]
